claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context! So you're inquiring about Child Benefit for your son **Alex**. 

Let me start gathering the information I need. Here's my first question:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Alex is 6 years old.

**Are you the parent or guardian of Alex, and do you have parental responsibility for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. 

**What is your current residency status? Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen living here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that information.

**Are you currently living in the UK with Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I live in the UK - I'm in Leeds - but Alex doesn't actually live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

**Can you tell me more about where Alex is currently living and why he's not with you? For example, is he living with another parent, a relative, or in another arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's helpful to know.

**Does Alex live with his other parent in the UK, or outside the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they live in the UK as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Are you providing financial support for Alex, and if so, what is the nature and amount of that support?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not currently contributing financially - things have been quite tight for me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, thank you for being honest about that.

**Just to clarify: does the other parent of Alex currently claim Child Benefit for him, or are they not claiming it either?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure if they're claiming it or not, to be honest.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's understandable. Let me ask you a couple more questions to get a complete picture.

**What is your current employment status? Are you working, unemployed, or in another situation?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm working at the moment, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Roughly what is your annual income from your employment?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd say around £35,000 a year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that figure.

**One more important question: are you a resident of the UK for tax purposes, and have you lived in the UK for at least two of the last three years?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I've lived here all my life - definitely more than two of the last three years!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I now have enough information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the situation: You are a British citizen living in the UK, and you have parental responsibility for Alex, who is 6 years old and also lives in the UK. However, Alex is not currently living with you—he's living with his other parent. Additionally, you're not currently providing financial support for Alex.

Under UK Child Benefit rules, the person who can claim Child Benefit is typically the person who is responsible for and living with the child. Since Alex is living with his other parent rather than with you, you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. The other parent, as the person with whom Alex is residing, would be the appropriate person to claim.

Let me report this outcome for you:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to be the bearer of disappointing news, but unfortunately you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex at this time, because he is not living with you. 

However, this doesn't mean the Child Benefit goes unclaimed—the other parent, with whom Alex is living, would be able to claim it. If you'd like more information about Child Benefit or have any other questions, I'm happy to help.

The other parent would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit for Alex.">
